title: Session Claims
description: The claims a Mentora API session carries, and the only source of the tenant/role/capability a request is authorized as (V0-021). A request's own fields may never supply a tenant: `institution_id` here is derived from the session record and is what every repository call is scoped by (docs/security/IDENTITY_AUTHORIZATION_AND_TOKENS.md, "Every request validates tenant/course/class/resource"). `scopes` is the intersection of what the session was issued with and what the account's role currently grants, so narrowing a role takes effect on the next request rather than at expiry. The credential mechanism is not a decided technology (the canonical architecture names institutional federation; no ADR accepts an implementation), so `authenticator` is required to name the capability that issued the session, and a stand-in must say so through `capability_kind`.

aud.description: A session authorizes the API, not the media plane; the media plane gets a bootstrap token or a floor token.

jti.description: The session id (auth_sessions.session_id); revocation is recorded against it.

institution_id.description: The tenant. A session claim, never a request field, so a caller cannot widen its own scope by naming one.

account_id.description: The account this session is for.

role.description: The canonical role name (governance/TERMINOLOGY_REGISTRY.yaml). The spec's wider role list (institution admin, IT operator, moderator, auditor, …) is not yet modelled.

scopes.description: Capabilities, not a role string: a guard is written against the absence of a capability. A session carries the intersection of what it was issued and the account's current role, so a role change can only remove a capability, never add one. `join` is the student's participant capability: a teacher holds no `join`, and a class join binds to the authenticated student's own account (DEC-TURN-001). Stored in a stable order so the same role always produces the same session row.

authenticator.description: name@version of the credential capability that issued the session, e.g. local-credentials@1.0.0.

capability_kind.description: DEVELOPMENT_MOCK marks a stand-in for an OPEN decision (DEC-TECH-*). It is never presented as the platform's authentication.

exp.description: Bounded lifetime. Revocation is the other terminal path; both are enforced on every read (DEC-RUNTIME-007).
